pending.n: Sarutahiko Coffee Imperial Palace East Gardens
pending.why: The first café ever inside the Imperial Palace grounds, opened 3 November 2026 in the new Ote rest area. It has its own East Gardens blend (~¥720) and garden-themed souvenirs. Open when the gardens are (closed Mondays and Fridays).
pending.halal: Coffee and cakes; no halal certification.

pending.why: Its name literally means "weird shop": a tiny store behind a torii gate on the 4th floor of Nakano Broadway, packed with pre-war tin toys, old signboards and toys up to the '80s. A museum where everything is for sale.

The only museum in the world for Osaka-Kyoto woodblock prints (mostly kabuki actors), hidden by Hozenji Yokocho a few minutes from Dotonbori. You can print your own ukiyoe. ~¥700, 11:00–18:00, closed Mondays.
Japan's first café inside a ZARA store, in the four-floor Shinsaibashi flagship: a Nara wood counter, cobblestone floor and saucers shaped like the old mokko flower. A coffee break mid-shopping.

The halal restaurant that served 180,000 people at Expo 2025 opened in Kyoto (Shijo Karasuma, SUINA Muromachi B1F) in July 2026, with halal-certified wagyu including Miyazaki's Arita wagyu. 11:00–22:00.
pending.halal: Fully halal, no alcohol (per Groovy Japan); halal-certified wagyu.

pending.why: A former izakaya turned halal yakiniku, 6 minutes from Ikebukuro's West Exit: A5 Miyazaki wagyu and halal lamb jingisukan. Daily 17:00–24:00, weekend lunch by booking.
pending.halal: Muslim-friendly with a halal menu (Halal Food in Japan trust score 3, not certified); ask about alcohol.

pending.why: A loved Showa-era kissaten in Motomachi that closed in 2025 and came back in January 2026, now run by the old Kobe roaster Nichibei Coffee. Retro morning sets until 11:00.
pending.halal: Coffee and toast; no halal certification.

pending.why: The Korean donut café with the twisted kkwabaegi donuts, made by hand every morning; new branches get queues of 150+ people. Seasonal flavours change often.
